speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the history. Given your fever and altered mentation, have you noticed any stiff neck, severe headache, or sensitivity to light?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient presents with a 2-day history of fever and altered mentation, reporting fever without chills and rigors. He denies sore throat, abdominal pain, headache, loose stool, burning micturition, or seizures. Has a history of tics and is currently taking haloperidol.

speaker: Doctor
text: I note your history of tics and haloperidol use; have you been adhering to your medication, and have you noticed any involuntary movements or muscle rigidity recently? REQUEST TEST: Complete_Blood_Count, Comprehensive_Metabolic_Panel.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Complete_Blood_Count: White_Blood_Cell_Count: 14,700/mm3 (elevated); Comprehensive_Metabolic_Panel: NORMAL READINGS

speaker: Doctor
text: Good news on the normal metabolic panel, but that elevated white blood cell count suggests an active infection or severe inflammatory process. Since you denied a headache, but we are still concerned about your altered mental status and fever, have you noticed any confusion, memory lapses, or hallucinations? REQUEST TEST: Serum_Electrolytes, Magnesium, Calcium, Phenytoin_Level.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Serum_Electrolytes: NORMAL READINGS; Magnesium: NORMAL READINGS; Calcium: NORMAL READINGS; Phenytoin_Level: NORMAL READINGS

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your normal electrolytes and medication levels, and considering your haloperidol use, are you experiencing any visual hallucinations or recent falls? REQUEST TEST: Toxicology_Screen, Brain_MRI.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the negative tox screen and unremarkable MRI, plus your haloperidol use and normal labs, have you been taking your medication as prescribed, and do you experience any involuntary movements like chorea or dystonia? REQUEST TEST: Serum_Dopamine_Binding_Assay, Serotonin_Level.
